title: Youtuber "Proves" People are Lazy with DayTrading
summary: Investigation of a forex guru promoted in a car YouTuber's day-trading stunt: course income dwarfs trading, simulated accounts, an offshore broker, and prop-firm conflicts.

assertions.quote: There's more money to make selling shovels in a gold rush than mining for gold.
it turns out doubling your money is actually very risky
No matter how much someone says they just know the trade is going to go up, they really don't.
Simulated just means essentially you're using monopoly money.

verdicts.note: Regulators require simulated-results disclaimers because the practice is common; prevalence is not measured.

assertions.quote: they make money when traders lose, which is strange when you think about it
a big part of forex scams are sketchy offshore brokerages where you don't know if it's real or fake money

verdicts.note: Regulator warning lists and enforcement actions document offshore forex broker fraud.

assertions.quote: he did admit that he has paid influencers in the past to collaborate

verdicts.note: Paid promotion of trading and crypto products by influencers is well documented and has drawn regulator action.

assertions.quote: even if you do win and you make a bunch of money, many of these companies will ban your accounts or delay your withdrawals

verdicts.note: Widely reported in complaints; prevalence is unmeasured.
